I farm only 4.1 mu by myself, so I will keep the whole field in the wheat-maize rotation that I already know well. I have done this for many years, and at my age I will choose a steady, familiar way rather than anything complicated. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on that to protect yield in dry periods, but I will still keep inputs moderate so the cost and labor stay manageable. For wheat, I will use an improved seed, do rotary tillage, put most fertilizer before or around sowing, irrigate two times, and spray only when I feel the field really needs it. For summer maize, I will plant hybrid seed after wheat harvest, keep the same 4.1 mu, use rotary tillage again because it saves labor, give enough nitrogen for grain filling, irrigate two times if needed, and keep pesticide use limited. What I want most is a stable harvest with work I can still handle myself.
